Human-Agent Principle Distillation

Yannick Fontan · Original text from the YouTube description.

Symbolic Reasoning Agent An experimental journey through ARC-AGI 3 Episode 2 • Official Game LS20 Human-Agent Principle Distillation

Last time, I introduced the vision behind this project. Today, I would like to challenge one of the most influential definitions of intelligence. François Chollet defines intelligence as the ability to efficiently adapt to new situations. I believe this definition can be pushed one step further. Because if a situation were truly, completely unknown... No familiar concepts. No familiar relationships. No familiar principles. ...then no intelligence could solve it efficiently. It would have no choice but to explore almost blindly. So when an intelligence adapts elegantly to something new... I don't believe it is because the situation is completely unknown. I believe it is because something inside that situation is already familiar. Not the situation itself. Its underlying structure.

This leads me to a slightly different definition. Intelligence is having both a rich enough structure of meaning and the ability to navigate it, so that every new situation can be connected to it and experienced as familiar. Knowledge alone is not enough. A dictionary contains knowledge. It does not understand. Intelligence requires structure. Relationships. Hierarchy. Meaning. And above all... The ability to create new connections.

This is exactly what today's video is about. As the agent explores this new version of LS20, it eventually reaches a situation it cannot solve. That failure is not the end of the reasoning process. It is the beginning. Together, the human and the agent analyze what happened. Not to invent a solution for this particular level... ...but to extract a general principle. A principle that could apply to many future worlds. I call this process Human-Agent Principle Distillation. Here is the loop: The symbolic reasoning agent executes and produces evidence. The human identifies a new principle. The coding agent integrates that principle into the architecture. And the cycle begins again. The goal is never to memorize a solution. The goal is to discover a reusable principle. Once that principle enters the symbolic knowledge base... The architecture itself becomes richer. Its structure of meaning expands. And tomorrow... Another unknown world becomes just a little more familiar.

This is not simply learning. It is the continuous construction of a structure of meaning. One principle at a time. One world at a time. One abstraction at a time. Because I believe that intelligence does not grow by accumulating experiences. It grows by organizing them into an ever more coherent structure of meaning.

"Every new principle makes tomorrow's unknown a little more familiar."
